sections.title: Optimal stability hierarchies of the Heisenberg Uncertainty Principle for solenoidal fields and of the second order Caffarelli--Kohn--Nirenberg inequalities
sections.abstract: The paper proves sharp stability hierarchies for the Heisenberg uncertainty principle for solenoidal fields and for a second-order Caffarelli--Kohn--Nirenberg inequality, with explicit constants, remainder terms, and equality cases.
sections.claimed_result: The authors state sharp stability constants in both settings and a hierarchy of remainder terms measuring distance to extremals, with a transformed one-dimensional proof and explicit extremals.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Solenoidal vector fields in dimension N and weighted second-order inequalities on 1+a+b=0, under the stated dimensional and parameter restrictions.
sections.caveat: ArXiv preprint; the abstract does not substitute for checking the lengthy stability and equality-case proofs.

sections.title: Completely monotone negative powers of hyperbolic polynomials
sections.abstract: The paper proves complete-monotonicity and positivity conjectures for negative powers of homogeneous hyperbolic polynomials and derives quantitative log-concavity and Gaussian-comparison bounds for associated Riesz kernels.
sections.claimed_result: The author states that every homogeneous half-plane-property polynomial has a completely monotone negative power, and that p^-alpha is completely monotone for alpha >= 4096n^2 under the stated assumptions.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: p is homogeneous and hyperbolic in n >= 2 variables and positive on its hyperbolicity cone; Riesz-kernel conclusions additionally assume pointed cone closure.
sections.caveat: Numerical constants and the specialized V'amos-quartic example are author claims in a preprint.

sections.title: Optimal regularity for the arrival time equation
sections.abstract: For convex mean-curvature flow, the paper establishes sharp regularity and asymptotic expansions for the singular arrival-time equation, including planar C^{24,alpha} regularity and the sharp higher-dimensional C^{2,2/n} result.
sections.claimed_result: The authors state C^{24,alpha} planar regularity with a logarithmic modulus at the 24th derivative, sharpness, arbitrary-order rescaled-flow expansions, and sharp C^{2,2/n} regularity in higher dimensions when combined with prior work.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Arrival-time functions from convex mean-curvature flow in R^{n+1}; planar and higher-dimensional statements differ.
sections.caveat: The higher-dimensional conclusion relies on Sesum's work and sharpness uses a companion preprint.

sections.title: Singularity models for the Bernoulli free boundary problem from isoparametric hypersurfaces
sections.abstract: The paper constructs homogeneous Bernoulli free-boundary solutions from isoparametric sphere foliations, producing new singularity models and a rigidity theorem determined by radial geometry.
sections.claimed_result: The authors state a general construction, geometric representation, and rigidity theorem, plus a density conjecture for non-flat cones in dimensions n >= 5.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Isoparametric foliations of the sphere and homogeneous one-phase/Bernoulli free-boundary solutions.
sections.caveat: The density assertion is explicitly a conjecture.

sections.title: Formal groups and (φ,Γ)-modules
sections.abstract: For formal modules over unramified p-adic extensions, the paper constructs a period ring and proves an equivalence between étale (φ,Γ)-modules and continuous Galois representations, recovering cyclotomic and Lubin--Tate cases.
sections.claimed_result: The author states an equivalence for finitely generated O_E-modules with continuous Gal_K action and étale (φ_E,Γ)-modules over R_{H,K}, plus a general equivalence for flat F-dynamical systems.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: K/E is a finite unramified extension of p-adic local fields and H is a one-dimensional formal O_E-module of finite height over O_K.
sections.caveat: The 81-page construction and its comparison with classical cases require specialist review.

sections.title: Fourier duality on compactified Prym fibrations
sections.abstract: The paper studies Fourier--Mukai duality for compactified Prym fibrations, obtaining consequences for motivic decompositions and multiplicativity of the perverse filtration.
sections.claimed_result: The author states a shadow of the Hausel--Thaddeus conjecture, a proof of the Corti--Hanamura motivic decomposition conjecture for the stated fibrations, and multiplicativity of the perverse filtration.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Compactified Prym fibrations, including SL Higgs-bundle moduli over the elliptic locus; the dual abelian fibration is treated as a stack.
sections.caveat: The scope is a specified class of fibrations and the abstract describes a partial consequence as a shadow.

sections.title: No Universal Remainder Rate for Chambolle-Dossal Acceleration
sections.abstract: The paper constructs smooth convex losses showing that Chambolle--Dossal acceleration has no universal rate improvement beyond o(n^-2), while identifying a sharp rate under a local p-power growth condition.
sections.claimed_result: For every alpha > 3 and divergent nondecreasing gain G, the authors construct a loss defeating the proposed universal gain; under local p-power growth they state the sharp rate n^{-2p/(p-2)}.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Exact Chambolle--Dossal orbits for fixed smooth convex losses with minimizers; the positive sharpness statement assumes local p-power growth and sufficiently strong damping.
sections.caveat: The impossibility concerns universality across losses, not all structured objectives; practical implications remain open.

sections.title: On Simon's area-minimizing hypersurfaces with fractal singular sets
sections.abstract: The paper verifies that Leon Simon's stable minimal hypersurfaces with prescribed fractal singular sets are area-minimizing.
sections.claimed_result: The author states that Simon's examples are area-minimizing, establishing existence of area-minimizing hypersurfaces with fractal singular sets.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The stable minimal hypersurfaces constructed by Simon with prescribed singular sets.
sections.caveat: The concise abstract leaves the inherited hypotheses and verification scope to the paper.
